Main.sentence: Barack Hussein Obama Sr. ( /ˈbærək huːˈseɪn oʊˈbɑːmə/ ;   born Baraka Obama , 18 June 1934   – 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , the ___E:44th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ .
He is a central figure of his son's memoir, Dreams from My Father (1995).
Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia.

He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the ___E:University of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawaii)___ where he met ___E:Stanley Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham)___ , whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack.
Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.

Obama then went to ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ for graduate school, where he earned an M.A. in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama Sr. married ___E:Ruth Beatrice Baker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Beatrice_Baker)___ , a ___E:Jewish-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews)___ woman he had met in Massachusetts.
They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport.
He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the ___E:Ministry of Finance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance_(Kenya))___ .
He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ .

Obama Sr. had conflicts with ___E:Kenyan president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Kenya)___ ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ , which adversely affected his career.

He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama Sr. was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

Barack Obama Sr. was born in 1934   in ___E:Rachuonyo District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachuonyo_District)___  on the shores of ___E:Lake Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria)___ just outside ___E:Kendu Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendu_Bay)___ , ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ , at the time a colony and protectorate of the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ .

He was raised in the village of ___E:Nyang'oma Kogelo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang%27oma_Kogelo)___ , ___E:Siaya District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siaya_District)___ , Nyanza Province.
His family were members of the ___E:Luo people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people)___ .

His father was ___E:Onyango Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyango_Obama)___ , and his mother was ___E:Habiba Akumu Nyanjango U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akuma_Obama)___ (c. 1918–2006) of ___E:Karabondi, Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachuonyo_Constituency)___ , Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Barack Sr., they had two daughters.
After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, ___E:Sarah Ogwel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Onyango_Obama)___ of Kogelo.

As a young man, Onyango enlisted in the ___E:British Colonial Auxiliary Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Colonial_Auxiliary_Forces)___ and visited ___E:Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe)___ , ___E:India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj)___ and ___E:Zanzibar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanzibar)___ where he converted from ___E:Roman Catholicism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ to ___E:Orthodox Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam)___ , changing his name to Hussein.

The Times alleged, based on statements from his third wife ___E:Sarah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Onyango_Obama)___ , that Onyango was jailed by British colonial authorities during the ___E:Mau Mau rebellion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_rebellion)___ after being suspected of supplying information to ___E:Kenya Land and Freedom Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Land_and_Freedom_Army)___ (KFLA) insurgents and was subject to abuse while imprisoned which resulted in several physical scars and made him "loathe the British".

However, in his 2012 biography of Barack Obama, American writer David Maraniss claimed that Onyango did not support the KFLA during the Mau Mau rebellion and wasn't imprisoned by the British, and continued to be trusted by colonial authorities.

When Obama Sr. was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to ___E:Anglicanism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Church_of_Kenya)___ when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from " ___E:Baraka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barakah)___ " to " ___E:Barack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_(disambiguation))___ ".
He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.
While still living near ___E:Kendu Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendu_Bay)___ , Obama Sr. attended Gendia Primary School.
After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.

From 1950 to 1953, he studied at ___E:Maseno National School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maseno_School)___ , an exclusive Anglican boarding school in ___E:Maseno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maseno)___ .
The head teacher, B.L.
Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly.
Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."  In 1954 at age 20, Obama Sr. married ___E:Kezia Aoko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kezia_Obama)___  in a tribal ceremony in Kenya.
They had two children, ___E:Malik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Obama)___ (a.k.a. Roy) and ___E:Auma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auma_Obama)___ .
In 1959, the Kenyan Department of Education published Obama's monograph, entitled Otieno jarieko.
Kitabu mar ariyo. 2: Yore mabeyo mag puro puothe. (English: Otieno, the wise man. Book 2: Wise ways of farming. )
Due to his accomplishments, in 1959 Obama received a scholarship in economics through a program organized by the nationalist leader ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ .
The program offered education in the West to outstanding Kenyan students.

Initial financial supporters of the program included ___E:Harry Belafonte U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Belafonte)___ , ___E:Sidney Poitier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Poitier)___ , ___E:Jackie Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Robinson)___ , and ___E:Elizabeth Mooney Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Mooney_Kirk)___ , a literacy advocate who provided most of the financial support for Obama's early years in the United States.

Kirk and her literacy associate ___E:Helen M. Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_M._Roberts)___ of ___E:Palo Alto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California)___ raised the money necessary for Obama to travel to the US.
When Obama left for the United States, he left behind his young wife, Kezia, and their baby son Malik.
Kezia was pregnant, and their daughter Auma was born while her father was in Hawaii.

At Obama's request, ___E:Helen M. Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_M._Roberts)___ committed to watching over and financially supporting the family that he had left behind, for as long as she remained in Nairobi.

In 1959, Obama enrolled at the ___E:University of Hawaii at Manoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawaii_at_Manoa)___ in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ as the university's first African foreign student.

He initially lived across the street from the university at the Charles H. Atherton branch of the ___E:YMCA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YMCA#Residences)___ at 1810 University Avenue;  public records from 1961 indicate he later had a residence two miles southeast of the university at 625 11th Avenue in the ___E:Kaimuki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaimuki)___ neighborhood.

In 1960, Obama met ___E:Stanley Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham)___ in a basic ___E:Russian language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ course at the University of Hawaii and they started dating.
After becoming pregnant, Dunham dropped out of the University of Hawaii after the fall 1960 semester, while Obama continued his education.

Obama married Dunham in ___E:Wailuku U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wailuku,_Hawaii)___ on the Hawaiian island of ___E:Maui U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui)___ on 2 February 1961, despite parental opposition from both families.
He eventually told Dunham about his previous marriage in Kenya, but said he was divorced—which she found out years later was not true.

Their son, future US president ___E:Barack Obama II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , was born in Honolulu on 4 August 1961 at the former Kapiolani Maternity and Gynecological Hospital (succeeded by the ___E:Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapi%27olani_Medical_Center_for_Women_and_Children)___ ).

His birth was announced in The Honolulu Advertiser and the Honolulu Star-Bulletin, with his parents' address listed as 6085 Kalanianaole Highway in the Kuliouou neighborhood of Honolulu, seven miles east of the university—the rented home of Dunham's parents, ___E:Stanley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham)___ and ___E:Madelyn Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelyn_Dunham)___ .

Soon after her son's birth, Dunham took the infant with her to ___E:Seattle, Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle,_Washington)___ , where she took classes at the ___E:University of Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Washington)___ from September 1961 to June 1962.
Obama Sr. continued his education at the University of Hawaii and in 1961–1962 lived one mile east of the university in the St. Louis Heights neighborhood.

He graduated from the University of Hawaii after three years with a ___E:B.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ in ___E:economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics)___  and was elected to ___E:Phi Beta Kappa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa)___ .
He left Hawaii in June 1962.

Obama Sr. was offered a scholarship to study in New York City,  but declined it.  In September 1962, after a tour of ___E:mainland U.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States)___ universities, Obama Sr. traveled to ___E:Cambridge, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts)___ , where he began a graduate fellowship in economics at ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ .
He rented an apartment in a rooming house near ___E:Central Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Square_(Cambridge))___ in Cambridge.

Meanwhile, Dunham and their son returned to Honolulu in the latter half of 1962.  In January 1964, Dunham filed for divorce in Honolulu which was not contested by Obama;   they were divorced on 20 March 1964, whereupon Ann Dunham was granted sole custody of their son.

Obama was forced to leave his ___E:PhD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PhD)___ program at Harvard University in May 1964 because of administrators' concerns over his finances and personal life, including uncertainty over the number of wives he had, but he received an ___E:M.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts)___ in ___E:economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics)___ from Harvard in 1965.      In June 1964, Obama met and began dating a 27-year-old ___E:Jewish-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_American)___ elementary school teacher named ___E:Ruth Beatrice Baker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Ndesandjo)___ , the daughter of prosperous ___E:Lithuanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_Jews)___ immigrants to the United States.

After graduating from Harvard, Obama returned to Kenya in 1964.  [clarification needed] Baker followed him, and they married 24 December 1964.  They had two sons together, ___E:Mark Okoth Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ndesandjo)___ in 1965 and ___E:David Opiyo Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ndesandjo)___ in 1968.  Baker and Obama separated in 1971,   and divorced in 1973.   Baker subsequently married a Tanzanian man named Ndesandjo and took his surname, as did her sons Mark and David.
Mark said in 2009 that Obama had been abusive to him, his late brother David, and their mother.
In Kenya, Obama Sr. reconnected with his first wife Kezia.

She had two sons after his return: ___E:Abo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abo_Obama)___ (b. 1968) and ___E:Bernard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Obama)___ (b. 1970), believed to be his children.
Barack Obama, in his memoir Dreams from My Father (1995), said that his father's family had questioned whether Abo and Bernard are Barack Sr.'s biological sons.
Obama first worked as a government economist for an oil company in Kenya.

In 1965, Obama published a paper entitled "Problems Facing Our Socialism" in the East Africa Journal, harshly criticizing the blueprint for national planning, " ___E:African Socialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Socialism)___ and Its Applicability to Planning in Kenya", developed by ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ 's Ministry of Economic Planning and Development.
Obama considered the document to be not adequately socialist and African.
Obama served as an economist in the Kenyan Ministry of Transport.
Later he was promoted to senior economist in the Kenyan Ministry of Finance.
In 1970, Obama was in a serious automobile accident, and was hospitalized for nearly a year. In December 1971, he traveled to Hawaii for a month.
There he visited with his ex-wife Ann Dunham and American son Barack II, who was nearly 10. The visit was the last time the boy saw his father.

During his trip, Obama took his son to his first ___E:jazz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz_music)___ concert, a performance by the pianist ___E:Dave Brubeck U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Brubeck)___ .
His son recalled Obama giving him his first basketball:

I only remember my father for one month my whole life, when I was 10. And it wasn't until much later in life that I realized, like, he gave me my first basketball and it was shortly thereafter that I became this basketball fanatic.
And he took me to my first jazz concert and it was sort of shortly thereafter that I became really interested in jazz and music.

So what it makes you realize how much of an impact [even if it's only a month] that they have on you. But I think probably the most important thing was his absence I think contributed to me really wanting to be a good dad, you know?
Because I think not having him there made me say to myself, "You know what?
I want to make sure my girls feel like they've got somebody they can rely on."

According to Barack II's memoir, Obama's continuing conflict with ___E:Kenyan president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Kenya)___ ___E:Jomo Kenyatta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta)___ destroyed his career.
He came under suspicion after ___E:Tom Mboya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya)___ was assassinated in 1969, as he had been a protege of the ruler.

Kenyatta fired Obama, who was ___E:blacklisted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacklist)___ in Kenya and found it impossible to get work. By the time Obama visited his son in Hawaii in 1971, he had a bad leg from the 1970 accident.
Obama later broke both legs and shattered his knee cap in a second serious automobile accident, and subsequently lost his job.  His life deteriorated as he struggled with poverty and drinking.
During his final decade, he never recovered his former social or economic standing.

His friend Philip Ochieng, a journalist of the Kenya newspaper Daily Nation, has described Obama's difficult personality and drinking problems. [citation needed] In 1982, Obama had a relationship with Jael Otinyo and with her fathered his last son, named ___E:George Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_of_Barack_Obama#George_Hussein_Onyango_Obama)___ .

George was raised by his mother, who later remarried; his stepfather cared for him as well.  Six months after George's birth, Obama died in a car crash in ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ .
He was interred in his native village of ___E:Nyang'oma Kogelo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang%27oma_Kogelo)___ , ___E:Siaya District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siaya_District)___ .

His funeral was attended by ministers ___E:Robert Ouko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Ouko_(politician))___ , ___E:Peter Oloo-Aringo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Oloo-Aringo)___ , and other prominent political figures.
